title: mp blend
parentNote: Another blend today — two letters, two sounds, said almost on top of each other: mp, as in camp. It lives on the end of words, so the trouble is the same as it was with nd: the last sound gets dropped and "camp" comes out "cam", "lamp" comes out "lam". The fix is physical. Both sounds happen with the lips shut, so have your child press their lips together, hum the m, and then pop them open for the p — mmm-p. Once they can feel the pop they stop leaving it off. Say the word at normal speed straight afterwards so it doesn't get stuck sounding like two words.

activities.mouthCue: Shut your lips and hum for m, then pop them open for p. Both sounds happen in the same place.
activities.prompt: This pair is not like sh or ch. Here you really do hear both letters — they are just in a hurry.

lines: Tim and Pam did camp on the sand.
Pam had ham and chips in a big bag.
A damp chimp did romp in and chomp on the ham!
Tim ran at the chimp and it ran off.
Tim did lock the bag in the van.
